Military tensions between Russia and Ukraine continued to rise as thousands of Russian troops gathered near the Ukrainian border. Western intelligence agencies reported large movements of tanks, artillery and missile systems toward several strategic locations close to Ukraine.
Ukrainian officials warned that the buildup could signal preparations for a possible invasion. NATO leaders urged Russia to de-escalate the situation and return to diplomatic negotiations.
Meanwhile, residents in eastern Ukraine reported an increase in ceasefire violations along the contact line separating Ukrainian forces and Russian-backed separatists. International observers expressed concern that the growing tensions could lead to a broader conflict in the region.

Russian forces launched a large-scale military invasion of Ukraine early Thursday, attacking multiple cities with missile strikes and ground troops. Explosions were reported in the capital Kyiv as Ukrainian air defenses attempted to intercept incoming missiles.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declared martial law and called on citizens to defend the country. Russian troops advanced from several directions, including the north through Belarus and from the eastern region of Donbas.
International leaders condemned the attack and announced plans to impose economic sanctions on Russia. Military analysts say the invasion marks the largest military conflict in Europe in decades.

As the fighting in Ukraine entered its third week, humanitarian organizations warned of a growing crisis for civilians trapped in war zones. Thousands of families have fled major cities as airstrikes and artillery bombardments damaged homes, hospitals and schools.
The United Nations reported that millions of refugees had crossed into neighboring countries, including Poland and Romania. Emergency aid groups are struggling to provide food, shelter and medical assistance to displaced populations.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces continued to resist Russian advances in several cities, slowing the pace of the invasion. However, analysts say the prolonged conflict could deepen the humanitarian disaster if fighting continues.

After weeks of intense fighting, Russian and Ukrainian negotiators resumed diplomatic talks aimed at reaching a ceasefire agreement. Officials from both countries met in Istanbul to discuss possible compromises that could end the conflict.
Negotiators focused on proposals involving security guarantees for Ukraine and the withdrawal of certain military forces. While both sides acknowledged progress in the discussions, major disagreements remain.
International leaders encouraged continued dialogue, arguing that diplomacy offers the best path to ending the war and preventing further humanitarian suffering.

Global attention has increasingly shifted toward rebuilding Ukraine and supporting long-term recovery after months of conflict. International organizations and governments are discussing plans to fund reconstruction of damaged infrastructure, including roads, schools and energy systems.
Economic experts estimate that the cost of rebuilding Ukraine could reach hundreds of billions of dollars. Several countries have pledged financial assistance and humanitarian aid.
Although fighting continues in some eastern regions, policymakers say the focus is gradually moving toward post-war recovery and regional stability.
